articles.title: 'She masked, she masked, she masked': Unseen autism and its toll on young girls
articles.summary: Why delayed diagnosis of autism in young girls puts their mental health at risk.
articles.body:
Ruby Hobbs-Leffler felt things with an intensity that even a smart little girl with a big vocabulary couldn't put into words.

Life was an onslaught of bright lights, loud noises, intolerable textures and tastes. Feelings bubbled up uncontrollably: inconsolable howls in infancy, classroom meltdowns in childhood, rages in adolescence.

Most children did not understand her. Neither did many adults. She was articulate and insightful in so many ways — why wouldn't she just behave? No one seemed to understand the world was sometimes too much for Ruby. What she absorbed instead, her mother, Jessica Leffler, said, was that she was too much: too dramatic, difficult, strange.

Her diagnosis with autism at age 14 was, to Ruby, a relief. There were reasons for the way she perceived things, words for the sensory experiences that set her apart from peers.

Leffler was angry. Why did Ruby have to go so many years without the support she needed? Why did none of the professionals the family asked for help identify her needs? Why did she spend the formative years of her life being treated by teachers and peers like a failure, instead of a person navigating a world designed for a different way of thinking?

And today, after Ruby's 2024 death from suicide at age 15, she wants to know: Why are so many autistic girls with gifts and challenges like Ruby being overlooked?

Autistic children are significantly more likely than their neurotypical peers to have co-occurring mental health conditions like depression and anxiety, and to think about and die by suicide.

For girls, however, there is an additional complicating layer.

Autistic girls without co-occurring intellectual disabilities tend to be diagnosed significantly later than their male counterparts, often not until adolescence or later. As a result, they miss out on early interventions that can help neurodivergent children navigate challenging environments. They are more likely to be diagnosed with psychiatric disorders like depression or anxiety before their autism is identified, and often feel little relief from interventions designed for neurotypical people.

Many cope by masking or camouflaging — suppressing autistic traits in order to fit in. Without the right support, what starts as unconscious mimicry of peers' behavior in childhood can exact a painful toll as time goes on.

There is no single reason why anyone dies by suicide, no way of knowing if any alternative step would have led to a different outcome. But Leffler feels strongly that being understood sooner might have buoyed Ruby during her lowest points.

"It is so incredibly hard to live life the way that Ruby lived life," Leffler said recently at her dining table in Princeton, Kan. It was strewn with photos of Ruby cuddling cats and grinning at the camera, notebooks full of her drawings and color-coded homework.

"She masked, she masked, she masked," Leffler said. "And that's exhausting."

Boys and girls are diagnosed with autism at roughly equal rates until about age 3. These youngest children typically have major language or developmental delays that are easier for parents and doctors to spot.

In the elementary school years, their trajectories diverge. Boys are diagnosed with the neurodevelopmental condition at more than three times the rate of girls, and at younger ages.

Boys are more likely to receive their autism diagnosis between the ages of 3 and 11, one 2024 review of electronic health records found. Girls are typically diagnosed before age 3 or after age 11.

Researchers say that skewed ratio may be self-perpetuating: Because more boys are thought to have autism, diagnostic tools are biased toward boys' autistic traits.

"Girl autism really does not check the behavioral boxes that we, as clinicians and researchers, have been taught to look for," said Lauren Kenworthy, chief of neuropsychology and director of the Center for Autism Spectrum Disorders at Children's National in Washington, D.C.

Boys are more likely than girls to display autistic traits like lack of eye contact and repetitive motions such as rocking or hand-flapping. They tend to play alone more often than their female peers.

Girls tend to be more adept at mimicking social responses like eye contact and reciprocal play. They have deep, all-consuming special interests just like autistic boys, but their preferred subjects are often socially mainstream: unicorns, a particular type of doll.

When they have intense reactions to changes in routine, uncomfortable situations or overwhelming stimuli — a response known as an autistic meltdown — parents, teachers and professionals may assume they are an unusually emotional neurotypical kid.

Ruby saw therapists for sleep and behavioral issues starting at age 9. Though she showed many classic early childhood indicators — sensitivity to noise, extremely limited food preferences, rigid adherence to routine and difficulties understanding social nuances — no one suggested she was autistic.

"I assumed, very incorrectly, that they would tell me what I needed to know," Leffler said.

Autistic kids often have "spiky" cognitive profiles, meaning that exceptional ability or maturity in some areas — verbal skills, for example, or reasoning — live alongside significant delays in areas like executive functioning and impulse control. Without that piece of information, adults and kids alike may not understand why a child who excels academically struggles with seemingly simpler tasks.

Girls' coping strategies often work until early adolescence. At that point, when female social relationships become exponentially more complicated and masking becomes more difficult, their mental health outcomes split sharply from those of their male peers.

In a study Kenworthy led earlier this year, researchers tracked 313 autistic youth ages 2 to 25. They noted higher rates of anxiety, depression and executive functioning challenges compared to non-autistic peers in both boys and girls throughout childhood. But in the teenage years, the girls' anxiety increased significantly over the boys', and remained elevated into adulthood.

The girls in Kenworthy's study already had autism diagnoses. For those who have not been identified, negative feedback from adults and peers can further depress self-esteem.

"Often, the longer a girl goes without knowing she has autism, the more deeply entrenched are her own negative attributions about her failings," Kenworthy said.

A 2024 review of Duke University hospital records found that girls diagnosed later with autism were also likely to have first received a diagnosis of depression or anxiety in the previous two years.

"When you are receiving these anxiety and mood diagnoses ... that's going to delay your [autism] diagnosis," said study author Dr. Matthew Engelhard, a Duke biostatistician.

Those challenges often persist into adulthood. Autistic people of all genders often struggle with nuances of social communication like decoding nonverbal cues, identifying shifts in tone or asking reciprocal questions. Women, however, often face higher social penalties if they don't hit those marks.

"There are different social standards for women, and this is why women mask harder," said Storee Powell, 38, a disability advocate in Smithfield, Utah.

Masking is not unique to autism and is not always harmful, Kenworthy pointed out. People often act more formally in job interviews than they do with friends, for example. But for many autistic women, masking is a relentless pressure that is associated with suicidal behavior over the long term.

In the general population, men die by suicide at significantly higher rates than women. Autistic women, however, die by suicide at about the same rates as autistic men, and at significantly higher rates than non-autistic women.

After her daughter Maisa, 13, attempted suicide in May 2023, Samia McCall began reading about neurodiversity. She was stunned how closely autism's description fit her creative, sensitive girl — her strong need for routine, social anxiety, challenges with communication and sensory processing.

She brought her findings to Maisa's doctor and therapist in Boise. They brushed off her concerns, she said, citing Maisa's good grades, verbal sophistication and empathy as evidence that she couldn't be autistic.

Maisa was on a six-month waitlist for a formal diagnosis when she died by suicide in November 2023 at age 14. While it's impossible to know what effect an evaluation would have had, McCall said, she believes her daughter would have benefited from earlier diagnosis.

"I think it could have made a huge difference in her self-esteem. I think she was internalizing a lot of things as a personal failure when just her brain was working differently," she said.

After connecting online last year, McCall, Leffler and a third grieving mother named Deborah Royal launched the Seen Movement , a suicide prevention organization advocating for change in systems' response to people in crisis.

"By the time you get to where someone's suicidal, it's like Stage IV cancer. You need an intervention early," McCall said. "Because if you identify and support someone who's autistic or neurodivergent early in life, then they're never going to develop this idea that something's wrong with them."

A childhood diagnosis doesn't guarantee that an autistic person will never grapple with depression, self-doubt or suicidal thoughts. But there is some evidence that the earlier a girl understands herself, the sooner she can design a life that works with her strengths and needs.

Anne Kirby, an assistant professor at Trinity College Dublin, has conducted extensive interviews with autistic adults in her research on autism and suicide. Multiple women diagnosed later in life told her the diagnosis alleviated some of the shame and confusion they felt about their differences. Once they understood why they found certain situations challenging, it was easier to give themselves permission for things like rest and breaks from sensory stimulation.

"A common experience of late-diagnosed people is that they generally feel that they hadn't received support for things that they were struggling with throughout their lives," Kirby said. "After diagnosis, they often were able to give themselves more freedom to live life differently."

Ruby thrived after her diagnosis. She excelled at online learning, which she could do quietly from a corner in Leffler's office, and was well-liked at the grocery store and doughnut shop where she worked. She planned to pursue a career in finance and marry a man who would agree to live at her mother's house forever, Leffler recalled with a laugh.

Then a complicated storm of medical, mental and personal crises struck in early 2024. As loved ones rallied to her side, she suffered increasingly serious mood swings, disordered eating and suicidal thoughts. Mental health providers dismissed her autism diagnosis as an irrelevant detail. She died on July 11, 2024, after a sudden, impulsive moment on an otherwise normal day.

Much later, Leffler found a tattoo artist with dimples like her daughter's and a studio painted Ruby's favorite shade of pink. Her arms today are as colorful as Ruby's notebooks: a collage of her favorite animals and objects, reproductions of her drawings, flowers in the shape of her handprint.

Ruby was perfect just the way she was, Leffler said. She doesn't want any other girl like her daughter to doubt that about herself.

"She was a bright, cuddly, sparkly person," Leffler said. "She deserves to be loved and missed."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.summary: Com a seca no Amazonas, o DNIT realiza obras de dragagem e desobstrução em pontos críticos para manter o transporte de passageiros e mercadorias em todo o estado.
articles.body:
Dragagem no Rio Amazonas é alvo de ação do MPF — Foto: Divulgação

O Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes (Dnit) vai iniciar, na primeira quinzena de setembro, obras de dragagem em quatro trechos de rios no Amazonas. A medida visa garantir a navegação de barcos e o transporte de passageiros e mercadorias durante o período de estiagem no estado.

As ordens de serviço já foram assinadas e a mobilização de equipes e equipamentos está em andamento.

As intervenções fazem parte do Plano Anual de Dragagem de Manutenção Aquaviária (PADMA), que prevê contratos com duração de cinco anos para ações preventivas contínuas.

Para a realização dos serviços, as equipes utilizarão o método de sucção e remoção de sedimentos. Já no trecho entre Manaus e Itacoatiara, o departamento empregará uma embarcação especial do tipo draga Hopper, adequada para grandes volumes de resíduos.

articles.title: VÍDEOS mostram inundação que atingiu o Grand Canyon, nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Autoridades buscam nesta segunda (31) por desaparecidos, e dezenas já foram resgatados. Enchente ocorreu após uma série de tempestades que atingiram a região durante o final de semana.
articles.summary: Autoridades buscam nesta segunda (31) por desaparecidos, e dezenas já foram resgatados. Enchente ocorreu após uma série de tempestades que atingiram a região durante o final de semana.
articles.body:
Vídeos compartilhados nas redes sociais mostraram a força da inundação que atingiu o Grand Canyon, nos Estados Unidos , no fim de semana.

A enchente repentina deixou um morto e entre 15 e 20 desaparecidos , segundo os órgãos que administram o parque natural. Os trabalhos de resgate estão em andamento nesta segunda-feira (31).

Nas imagens registradas por montanhistas, é possível ver rios de lama descendo em alta velocidade pelo Grand Canyon e arrastando detritos. Veja acima.

👉O Grand Canyon é um desfiladeiro de quase 1,5 mil metros de profundidade, localizado no Arizona e registrado oficialmente como Patrimônio Mundial de UNESCO. Suas rochas foram moldadas durante milhões de ano pela erosão do Rio Colorado.

As enchentes ocorreram após uma série de tempestades que atingiram a região durante o final de semana. Em uma região do Grand Canyon com declive acentuado, caiu até 2,5 centímetros de chuva em um intervalo de apenas 30 minutos , segundo o meteorologista Justin Johndrow, do Serviço Nacional de Meteorologia em Flagstaff —cidade próxima ao parque nacional.

O corpo de um homem de 46 anos foi encontrado às margens do rio Colorado, informou o serviço do do Grand Canyon. As autoridades ainda buscam localizar as pessoas desaparecidas.

Até o momento, 62 montanhistas foram retirados da região por via aérea , incluindo turistas que estavam hospedados no Phantom Ranch, um ponto comum de embarque e desembarque para praticantes de rafting, segundo o Serviço Nacional de Parques Nacionais dos EUA.

Enchente gerou buscas por desaparecidos no Grand Canyon — Foto: James Thompson/AP

A enchente arrastou grandes pedras, estruturas metálicas e outros detritos para o Rio Colorado. Montanhistas relataram que a força da água destruiu algumas passarelas e pontes no local.

“Isso nos lembra o quão dinâmica e ativa é a paisagem do Grand Canyon”, disse Jack Schmidt, diretor do Centro de Estudos do Rio Colorado na Universidade Estadual de Utah.

Alguns pontos turísticos populares do Grand Canyon foram fechados e excursões de rafting no rio Colorado foram suspensas temporariamente.

A montanhista Erica Viola contou que estava no acampamento Bright Angel quando a chuva começou na tarde de sábado (29), e que ela e cerca de 50 outros turistas viram o riacho subir e, em seguida, detritos começarem a ser arrastados pela correnteza, incluindo o que parecia ser um alojamento.

O grupo foi levado de helicóptero para um local seguro, encerrando sua aventura dois dias antes do previsto, segundo Viola.

articles.title: Tornado em Campo Erê (SC): fenômeno é investigado pela Defesa Civil  | G1
articles.standfirst: Tempestades vindas da Argentina avançaram rumo ao Brasil e chegaram na cidade do Oeste de Santa Catarina. Moradores registraram danos em telhados.
articles.summary: Imagens de radar do órgão mostram que a tempestade registrada na cidade de 9,6 mil habitantes teve sinal de rotação interna.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil de Santa Catarina analisa a possível passagem de um tornado em Campo Erê , no Oeste, na noite de domingo (30). Imagens de radar do órgão mostram que a tempestade registrada na cidade de 9,6 mil habitantes teve sinal de rotação interna .

O município registrou chuvas fortes e ventania por volta das 19h30 . O Corpo de Bombeiros atendeu moradores que tiveram os telhados danificados. Não há registro de feridos.

Uma foto divulgada pela Defesa Civil, feita pelo grupo Prevots, mostra a formação da tempestade (veja abaixo ). Procurada nesta segunda-feira (31), a prefeitura informou que ainda realiza o levantamento dos estragos .

Registro divulgado pela Defesa Civil mostra tempestade no interior de Campo Erê por volta das 19h26 — Foto: Grupo Prevots

🌪️ O tornado é caracterizado por uma coluna de ar em rotação que se estende da base de uma nuvem de tempestade até o solo, apresentando alto potencial destrutivo devido aos ventos intensos ( leia outros detalhes aqui ).

Segundo a Defesa Civil, tempestades severas se formaram sobre a província de Misiones, no norte da Argentina, e avançaram logo em seguida sobre o Extremo Oeste e Oeste catarinense. Com isso, cidades da região registraram granizo severo.

Essa mesma tempestade avançou para Campo Erê, mais precisamente ao sul da área urbana, por volta das 19h. Nas imagens do radar meteorológico de Chapecó ( veja abaixo ) é possível ver o sinal de rotação dentro da tempestade, compatível com a ocorrência de fenômenos associados a supercélulas.

"Os dados disponíveis até o momento apontam para a ocorrência de um tornado em Campo Erê. No entanto, para confirmação, a Defesa Civil do Estado irá realizar a avaliação do local, para verificar se há padrões de danos compatíveis com o fenômeno", informou o órgão.

Imagem divulgada pela Defesa Civil mostra radar reistrando tempestade severa — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

Consequências do mau tempo em Santa Catarina

O estado segue em alerta por conta da previsão de chuva forte até terça-feira (1º), segundo a Defesa Civil. Na sexta (28), uma mulher de 38 anos morreu após ser atingida por um raio . Entre o sábado (29) e esta segunda-feira (31), houve estragos em diversos municípios .

articles.title: Mulher volta para casa e encontra imóvel destruído por incêndio | G1
articles.standfirst: Vizinhos acionaram os bombeiros após perceberem o fogo na manhã desta segunda-feira (31). Moradora chegou depois do combate e disse não ter para onde ir.
articles.summary: Moradora não sabia do incêndio e chegou após o combate às chamas. Casa de madeira foi destruída pelo fogo e ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.body:
Depois de passar o fim de semana fora, Laura Montovani Martins voltou para casa na manhã desta segunda-feira (31) e encontrou o imóvel onde morava destruído por um incêndio, na Rua dos Ferroviários, no bairro Cabreúva, em Campo Grande. Ela não sabia que a casa havia pegado fogo e chegou quando os bombeiros já faziam o trabalho de rescaldo.

O fogo começou enquanto a moradora ainda estava fora. Vizinhos perceberam o incêndio e acionaram o Corpo de Bombeiros. Quando a equipe chegou ao endereço, as chamas estavam altas e a estrutura da casa de madeira já começava a desmoronar.

A moradora chegou somente depois que o fogo havia sido controlado. Ela não sabia do incêndio e encontrou os bombeiros fazendo o trabalho de rescaldo. Ao ver a casa destruída, chorou e disse não ter outro lugar para ficar.

“Eu não tenho para onde ir. E agora? O que eu vou fazer, meu Deus?”, disse.

Moradora se emociona ao encontrar casa destruída por incêndio no bairro Cabreúva, em Campo Grande — Foto: Caio Tumelero

A mulher contou que havia saído de casa no sábado e retornava após passar o fim de semana fora. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Segundo o soldado Monteiro, do Corpo de Bombeiros, a equipe levou cerca de seis minutos para chegar ao local após ser acionada. O cenário encontrado já era de um incêndio de grandes proporções.

“As labaredas estavam bem altas. Era uma casa de madeira, com bastante material combustível”, afirmou.

Cerca de 2,5 mil litros de água foram usados no combate. O fogo consumiu praticamente toda a estrutura de madeira e apenas a parte de alvenaria do banheiro permaneceu em pé.

A moradora disse não saber o que pode ter provocado o incêndio e afirmou que não havia deixado nenhum equipamento ligado antes de sair.

O Corpo de Bombeiros informou que a causa do fogo ainda é desconhecida.

articles.standfirst: Tragédia provocada pelo colapso de uma geleira deixou ao menos 919 mortos e 4.793 desaparecidos no Nepal e na China; autoridades iniciaram sepultamentos antes de concluir identificação.
articles.summary: Tragédia provocada pelo colapso de uma geleira deixou ao menos 919 mortos e 4.793 desaparecidos no Nepal e na China.
articles.body:
O Nepal começou nesta segunda-feira (31) a sepultar parte dos corpos recuperados após a avalanche que provocou uma enorme onda de gelo, pedras e detritos no Himalaia . A tragédia deixou pelo menos 919 mortos e milhares de desaparecidos no Nepal e na China .

No Nepal, as autoridades confirmaram 903 mortes e 4.247 desaparecidos na região atingida, próxima à fronteira com a China.

Familiares lotaram centros de resgate e hospitais em busca de informações sobre parentes desaparecidos. Outros tiveram de enfrentar a identificação de corpos em necrotérios improvisados e sobrecarregados.

Ao todo, 4.793 pessoas são consideradas desaparecidas nos dois países. Entre elas estão turistas e peregrinos que viajavam em direção ao Monte Kailash, considerado sagrado e localizado na região autônoma chinesa do Tibete .

No Nepal, 933 trabalhadores de usinas hidrelétricas estão entre os desaparecidos.

No último domingo (30), soldados e engenheiros do Exército nepalês perfuraram os escombros para tentar chegar a trabalhadores que podem ter ficado presos em um túnel de uma usina hidrelétrica no vale do rio Himalaia . As equipes conseguiram inserir um tubo no túnel para ajudar no resgate.

Trabalhadores que conseguiram escapar relataram cenas de destruição. Surendra Dowluri, de 33 anos, natural do estado indiano de Andhra Pradesh, disse que uma forte correnteza atingiu o local onde trabalhava.

"Ouvi­mos um som muito forte... e vimos que o andar da turbina estava submerso em lama. Seis trabalhadores ficaram presos ali", disse Dowluri à AFP após ser resgatado, quatro dias depois do desastre.

"Conseguimos resgatar cinco deles, mas uma pessoa morreu", afirmou. Segundo ele, outros trabalhadores conseguiram chegar a áreas mais altas ou a partes da usina que não foram atingidas pela correnteza.

O desastre começou com o colapso parcial de uma geleira. A grande quantidade de água e detritos transformou um rio em uma correnteza que avançou rapidamente pelo vale, segundo o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos.

No domingo, socorristas chineses que trabalhavam perto do porto fronteiriço de Gyirong, no Tibete, foram levados para uma área segura depois que um novo lago se formou devido a um deslizamento de terra, segundo a imprensa estatal chinesa.

No Nepal, o número de desaparecidos foi atualizado para 4.247 nesta segunda-feira (31). As autoridades confirmaram 903 mortes.

A quantidade de corpos recuperados e a falta de instalações adequadas para armazená-los fizeram as autoridades iniciarem os sepultamentos antes que todos fossem identificados.

Amostras de DNA foram coletadas dos corpos. A medida permitirá que os familiares façam a identificação posteriormente e realizem os rituais funerários tradicionais.

Familiares chegam aos centros de identificação e observam telas de LED com fotografias dos corpos encontrados. Em alguns casos, precisam fechar os olhos diante das imagens.

Shobha Adhikary disse a um coordenador em um necrotério improvisado que acreditava ter reconhecido seu melhor amigo de infância em uma das fotografias.

"Parece ele, com certeza", afirmou, enquanto mostrava aos coordenadores a imagem de um homem de meia-idade sorrindo.

Os sobreviventes agora enfrentam a tarefa de reconstruir suas vidas.

"Todos os vilarejos próximos do rio foram arrasados", disse à AFP Buddhi Ram Dangol, morador do distrito de Nuwakot, no Nepal. "Não sobrou nada."

O primeiro-ministro do Nepal, Balendra Shah, afirmou nas redes sociais que o país enfrenta um desastre "inimaginável e desolador". Segundo ele, o custo da reconstrução pode chegar a bilhões de dólares.

Shah também destacou o contraste entre os impactos sofridos pelo Nepal e sua contribuição para o aquecimento global. O país está entre os que têm menores emissões de carbono per capita no mundo.

O Nepal fica na região do Himalaia, a maior cadeia de montanhas do planeta. As geleiras da região estão derretendo em ritmo acelerado devido ao aumento das temperaturas.

As dificuldades de acesso à região atingida ficaram evidentes no domingo. Equipes chinesas que tentavam abrir uma rota até o epicentro da tragédia, próximo ao porto de Gyirong, avançaram apenas 285 metros.Nepal começa enterros após avalanche que matou 919 pessoas

articles.title: Em meio à formação de novo ciclone, Paraná pode ter ventos de 85 km/h; veja previsão do tempo | G1
articles.standfirst: Estimativa é da Climatempo. Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia emitiu alerta de tempestades para o estado.
articles.summary: Estimativa é da Climatempo. Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia emitiu alerta de tempestades para o estado.
articles.body:
Em meio à formação de um novo ciclone extratropical no Sul do Brasil, o Paraná pode registrar ventos em torno de 85 km/h nesta segunda-feira (31), segundo a Climatempo. A previsão é mais intensa para a metade sul e para o oeste do estado ; de acordo com os meteorologistas, quanto mais ao norte, mais brandos os temporais tendem a ser.

As rajadas podem ser acompanhadas de chuvas fortes e até mesmo granizo; por isso, o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu um alerta de tempestades para o estado.

Entre este domingo (30) e esta segunda-feira (31), temporais de granizo com pedras de gelo do tamanho de ovos de galinha já causaram estragos no Paraná.

A Climatempo ressalta que a segunda-feira (31) começou com tempo instável e que a chuva ganha força principalmente sobre o centro-sul do estado, com maior atenção para áreas do sudoeste, sul e região central. Veja a previsão do tempo por região mais abaixo.

"Os maiores volumes de chuva ficam concentrados no centro-sul. O risco de temporais se espalha por uma ampla faixa do Paraná, com níveis mais elevados de severidade no sul do estado. Nas áreas de maior risco, os temporais podem provocar chuva forte, raios e rajadas intensas, além da possibilidade de chuva persistente e volumosa".

O novo ciclone começa a se formar entre o fim do dia e a terça-feira (31) na altura de Santa Catarina, favorecendo a organização de uma nova frente fria e acelerando o avanço das instabilidades pelo Paraná.

🌀Os ciclones extratropicais são sistemas de baixa pressão atmosférica – regiões causadoras de tempo adverso em grande escala – que surgem normalmente em latitudes médias. Eles são formados pelo contraste de temperaturas de diferentes massas de ar (quente e fria).

Na terça (31) , a nova frente fria avança pelo Paraná e mantém o tempo bastante instável, principalmente durante a madrugada e a manhã. A chuva mais volumosa se concentra entre setores do centro do estado, Campos Gerais, Região Metropolitana de Curitiba e sul, com possibilidade de chuva forte e temporais em parte dessas áreas.

"Ao longo da tarde, a frente fria avança em direção ao Sudeste e as instabilidades começam a perder força em parte do Paraná. Mesmo assim, a chuva ainda pode persistir no leste, no litoral e na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba. A passagem do sistema também favorece o ingresso de ar mais frio, provocando uma queda expressiva das temperaturas em comparação com os dias anteriores. Palmas pode registrar mínima de apenas 6°C e General Carneiro, 7°C".

Na quarta-feira (2) a massa de ar frio associada a um sistema de alta pressão próximo ao oceano passa a dominar as condições do tempo no Paraná. A tendência é de estabilização em grande parte do estado, sem previsão de chuva, embora ainda haja possibilidade de chuva fraca e isolada no litoral devido à maior disponibilidade de umidade. As temperaturas podem chegar a 3ºC, segundo os meteorologistas.

"A quinta-feira (3) começa com tempo firme em todo o Paraná e presença de sol entre poucas nuvens. A manhã continua fria em várias áreas do estado. [...] A partir da tarde, as instabilidades voltam a aumentar no oeste, sudoeste e sul do Paraná. A mudança ocorre devido à atuação de um cavado em médios níveis da atmosfera associado a um sistema de baixa pressão no interior do continente. Há previsão de chuva fraca a moderada nessas áreas", diz a Climatempo.

O Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar) divulgou uma lista das estações meteorológicas que registraram rajadas de vento acima de 60 km/h desde o fim de semana. Veja abaixo.

articles.title: Nepal: resgate tenta chegar a mais de 900 pessoas presas em túneis | G1
articles.standfirst: Desastre natural que atingiu região dos Himalaias, na fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, matou mais de 900 pessoas e deixou quase 5 mil desaparecidos.
articles.summary: Desastre natural que atingiu região dos Himalaias, na fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, matou mais de 900 pessoas e deixou quase 5 mil desaparecidos.
articles.body:
Equipes de resgate do Nepal intensificaram os esforços nesta segunda-feira (31) para chegar até centenas de trabalhadores que estão presos em túneis de usina hidrelétrica. A entrada está bloqueada por uma espessa camada de lama, após a avalanche histórica que atingiu o país na última semana.

Os resgates ocorrem com a ajuda de especialistas chineses e indianos e se concentram nos túneis da usina Trishuli-3A que ficam nos distritos de Rasuwa e Chilime.

Autoridades nepalesas afirmaram que o objetivo é encontrar os 933 trabalhadores que estariam presos em 11 empreendimentos hidrelétricos, incluindo muitos em túneis, nos dois distritos mais atingidos, Rasuwa e Nuwakot.

Imagens divulgadas pelas equipes de resgate mostravam escavadeiras removendo lama e rochas sob refletores durante a noite. Em uma grande vala aberta no local, soldados usavam lanternas para procurar uma forma de entrar em um dos túneis

Equipes tentam chegar a mais de 900 trabalhadores presos em túneis de projeto hidrelétrico no Nepal em 31 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Ashish Gurung via Reuters

A avalanche sem precedentes de gelo, rochas, lama e detritos que atingiu a fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete na última quarta-feira matou mais de 900 pessoas e deixou quase cinco mil desaparecidos , segundo autoridades nepalesas e chinesas.

O desastre natural, atribuído ao colapso de uma geleira, deixou um rastro de destruição nas cidades e vilarejos da região.

No Nepal, 903 pessoas morreram e mais de 4,2 mil estão desaparecidos, segundo a última atualização dada pelas autoridades do país.

No Tibete, onde as informações são controladas pela China , o balanço oficial de mortos é de 16 e há 546 desaparecidos.

Centenas de corpos, muitos não identificados, foram enterrados em covas rasas , à medida que começaram a se decompor no clima úmido da região.

O exército nepalês informou que as equipes de busca e resgate estavam usando explosões controladas nos túneis, com escavadeiras e holofotes para remover a água e a lama e alcançar as pessoas presas. As equipes recuperaram três corpos após entrarem em dois túneis.

"Uma grande quantidade de detritos foi depositada, o que representa um grande desafio para a abertura dos túneis", disse Raja Ram Basnet, porta-voz do Exército nepalês, à agência de notícias Reuters. "Nosso foco principal é abrir os túneis".

Militares do Exército do Nepal retornam de uma operação de busca com os corpos de vítimas mortas nas enchentes em Bharatpur, no distrito de Chitwan, no Nepal. — Foto: Dar Yasin / AP

Avaliação dos danos é um desafio, diz premiê do Nepal

Nesta segunda (31), as autoridades nepalesas informaram que 903 pessoas morreram e 4.247 estão desaparecidas - incluindo as 933 que trabalhavam nos túneis dos empreendimentos hidrelétricos.

Do lado chinês, as autoridades disseram que 16 pessoas morreram no condado de Gyirong e outras 546 estão desaparecidas.

A Cruz Vermelha estimou que mais de 90 mil pessoas provavelmente foram afetadas pelo desastre, que a China atribuiu aos efeitos das mudanças climáticas.

O primeiro-ministro Balendra Shah afirmou que a inundação foi um "desastre natural devastador e sem precedentes" e que ainda é um desafio elaborar uma avaliação completa dos danos.

“Apesar do clima adverso, do terreno difícil e dos riscos contínuos, estamos avançando com determinação para salvar a vida de nossos cidadãos”, disse ele em uma publicação no Facebook no final do domingo, acrescentando que quase 21 mil agentes de segurança estavam envolvidos nas operações de resgate, além de trabalhadores civis e voluntários.

O presidente chinês Xi Jinping, em visita ao Quirguistão, afirmou que Pequim está fazendo todos os esforços para encontrar pessoas desaparecidas após o desastre, informou a agência Xinhua nesta segunda.

Pequim afirmou que 261 cidadãos estrangeiros de 23 países estavam desaparecidos no Tibete.

A emissora estatal chinesa CCTV informou que Pequim mobilizou mais de 2,1 mil socorristas e destinou pelo menos 220 milhões de yuans (cerca de R$ 169,7 milhões) para apoiar os esforços de socorro, além de ter lançado equipamentos e suprimentos por via aérea para os socorristas na linha de frente, enquanto seus soldados usavam equipamentos de detecção de sinais vitais para procurar os desaparecidos.

Embora o Nepal tenha afirmado que não precisa de ajuda estrangeira para as operações gerais de busca e resgate, o país tem recorrido à expertise de seus vizinhos, Índia e China, em resgates em túneis.

As operações de resgate foram suspensas várias vezes devido ao mau tempo e às preocupações de que um lago formado na fronteira entre Nepal e China pudesse provocar novas inundações depois de começar a transbordar para os rios nepaleses.

A emissora estatal chinesa CCTV informou que as geleiras ao redor de uma cratera formada perto do local do colapso da geleira continuam sob risco de desabar. Imagens de drones mostraram diversos depósitos de deslizamentos de terra em ambas as margens do rio, o que representa risco de novos desabamentos e da formação de novos lagos, segundo a emissora.

articles.title: Autumn: When does it start and why are there three calendars?
articles.summary: Why are there three different dates for the start of autumn and who follows which date?
articles.body:
For most of us, autumn means falling leaves, shorter days, returning to school and the more modern tradition of pumpkin spice lattes popping up again.

But when does it officially begin? Well that depends on which calendar you follow.

Many will argue 1 September is the day the seasons change, and they are right according to the meteorological calendar.

However, in the ancient Celtic calendar we've already been in autumn since 1 August.

But it's different again for those following the astronomical calendar who say we won't officially be in autumn until 23 September.

So why do we have three calendars and in 2026 who is actually using them?

At the beginning of August, dozens of people gathered in a druid grove in County Kilkenny to celebrate Lúghnasadh - the start of autumn in the Celtic calendar.

The ritual was led by Eimear Burke, Chosen Chief of the Order of Bards, Ovates and Druids which has 30,000 members around the world.

"It's the early harvest. This is the time when the first corn is cut, the first wheat is cut, the first bread of the year, as it were."

"It also represents that life, death and rebirth motif. Something dies in order to be reborn."

Standing in a circle in the grove, they shared bread and wine and welcomed the changing of the season and the landscape "because within druidry we have that strong sense of interconnectedness with everything".

"It's about reminding us that we're harvesting some things, but we need to wait. We need to wait in stillness."

Fiona Byrne is a history curator at the Ulster Folk Museum, which follows the Celtic calendar for its events and exhibitions.

"It's the calendar when people had a much better relationship with the land. The seasons and the changes were obviously very important to how they worked the land."

She says for the ancient Celts it was "vitally important" to be prepared for the darker days of winter and to get the harvest in before All Hallows Eve, what we would call Halloween.

"There's lots of traditions that the roaming spirits would spoil anything left out."

Byrne says while some ancient Lúghnasadh traditions like making harvest knots have almost disappeared, others like bonfires have remained a staple of our modern autumn celebrations.

And when asked when she thinks autumn starts: "I think that's the big debate... and it just all comes down to what you want to follow yourself.

"I've got the dual identity. At the Folk Museum, it is 1 August, when I'm in home life, it's all about back to school."

The meteorological calendar is a much more modern phenomenon, evolving through the 20th century as scientists and climatologists discovered more about weather patterns around the globe.

Like the Celtic calendar, it is divided into 4 seasons, but it starts one month later on 1 September.

BBC NI weather presenter Barra Best says it allows forecasters to "compare one season with another and look back through decades of weather records".

"I use the meteorological calendar when putting current conditions into context - whether that's comparing this summer's temperatures with a long-term average, or looking at how a season compares with previous years."

That does not mean the weather suddenly changes when the calendar flips to 1 September.

"We can still have very summery weather well into meteorological autumn, or wintry conditions during spring. The calendar simply gives meteorologists a consistent framework for recording and comparing our climate."

One person keeping a close eye on the meteorological calendar is Gary Quinn, who is part of Northern Ireland's civil contingencies group.

The multi-agency body is responsible for planning emergency responses in the event of a major weather event.

As director of rivers operations within the Department for Infrastructure, his main concern this autumn is the potential for flooding.

"It's been a fairly dry summer, but we expect rivers to recover, so we'll be keeping an eye on our hydrometric stations to see how those rivers perform.

"We talk to our Met Office colleagues continuously to get information around what potentially might happen. And we're in an alert state of readiness."

September will also see the release of the named storms for 2026/2027.

Quinn says a named storm is "more serious" than normal rainfall activity and puts them on a "heightened state of awareness".

Remembering the severe flooding in south-eastern parts of Northern Ireland in autumn 2023 Quinn says: "These things do live long in the memory because they're quite hectic at the time and that's notwithstanding the problems that they've brought to communities or to the people that are severely impacted by flooding. We're working to try and mitigate that as best as possible."

While the meteorological and Celtic calendars are seasonal, the astronomical calendar is based on the earth's position in relation to the sun - so it is defined by two solstices and two equinoxes.

For Marc Sarzi, Head of Research at Armagh Observatory and Planetarium, autumn will therefore begin on 23 September.

"What really is an astronomical year? It is what we call a sidereal year. This is exactly how much time it takes for the earth to go around the sun, or where, we basically are in the same position with respect to distant stars.

"I'm an extragalactic astronomer. And we say that distant galaxies are like flowers - each have their seasons.

"For us, it's a continuous spectrum of when we can see objects at night and when we can't."

"You start to see Orion in late autumn. Orion is a distinct constellation that you can see with the three stars... the belt of Orion."

He also says to watch out for Venus shining brightly in the evenings.

"We are lucky in Northern Ireland. We have quite a lot of dark places... and you can see lots of stars, lots of constellations."

articles.title: North East shipbuilding archive hopes to preserve memories
articles.summary: While campaigners in the North East wait for funding for a museum, an online archive is launched.
articles.body:
The friends and families of former shipbuilders have been urged to record their stories before they are forgotten.

Bronwyn Mogie, 33, from Jarrow, has been leading the campaign to establish a shipbuilding heritage museum in South Tyneside , a former hotspot for the industry.

While plans and fundraising for the museum are in the early stages, Mogie feared many stories could be lost before a spade has been put in the ground.

To counter this, people across north-east England have been asked to sit down with loved ones who once worked in the shipyards to contribute to the Shipyard Heritage Museum's online living archive. The archive is open to stories from the rivers Tyne, Wear and Tees.

Generations of Mogie's family were involved in shipbuilding and her dad was part of the last generation of workers before the yards on the Tyne were closed.

She is working alongside Andrew Leslie, the great-great-great nephew of the founder of Hawthorn Leslie shipyard in Hebburn, which closed in the 1980s.

"We wanted to do it properly, have funding for it, but people are just getting older and it's just not possible," Mogie said.

"I don't know how long we'd have to wait for the funding."

Voice recordings, videos and photographs can be uploaded to the museum's website.

"Sit them down and then let them talk," she said.

"Time's running out. One day they're going to be all gone and we'll never be able to get them back."

She hopes listening to family members' stories will provide an opportunity for younger generations to learn more about their heritage and area's history.

articles.title: Unification Church: 'Moonies' church leader jailed for two years over bribery offences
articles.summary: Han Hak-ja, 83, gave South Korea's former first lady two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace, a court found.
articles.body:
The leader of the controversial Unification Church has been sentenced to two years in prison for bribing South Korea's former first lady and other political funding offences.

A court found that Han Hak-ja's church gave Kim Keon Hee, the wife of ousted President Yoon Suk Yeol, two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace, together worth 80 million won ($57,900; £42,500).

Earlier this year, Kim was sentenced to 20 months in jail for accepting bribes from the church.

Han, the 83-year-old widow of the Unification Church's founder Sun Myung Moon, had repeatedly denied the allegations, calling them "false".

A special counsel team appointed to the case said Kim received the luxury products from the church between April and July 2022, in exchange for business and political favours.

The prosecutors said the probe was the first time the authorities have confirmed the church's attempt at buying influence in politics, and released photos of $19m (£14m) worth of cash found in Han's personal safe.

South Korea's former first lady admitted to receiving Chanel bags, but said she later returned them without using them.

Kim made a public apology when she appeared for questioning last August: "I am truly sorry that a nobody like me has caused concern to the people."

The Unification Church, known formally as The Family Federation for World Peace and Unification, was founded in South Korea in the 1950s by Sun Myung Moon, who proclaimed himself the messiah.

The church is probably best known for the mass weddings where thousands of couples were married by Han and her late husband and founder Sun Myung Moon in a stadium.

Critics have described the group as "cult-like". Lawyers have accused it of coercing devotees, known colloquially as "Moonies" after its founder, to donate large sums of money. "Moonies" is a term used by critics that many church members find offensive.

The Unification Church had come under the spotlight in Japan after the assassination of the country's former leader Shinzo Abe . The alleged assassin blamed the group for bankrupting his family and held a grievance against Abe for allegedly promoting it.

The church has boasted extensive links to politicians in Seoul, Tokyo, and even in Washington. Various politicians sent video message to its 2021 event congratulating the church's new think tank.

The list included US President Donald Trump, former US Vice-President Mike Pence, Shinzo Abe, as well as the mayors of Seoul and Busan.

The group is banned in parts of the world, including Singapore. In Japan, it has been ordered to dissolve.

articles.title: 'Venezuela will be reborn': Maduro shares first photos from US prison since capture
articles.summary: US News: Two photographs posted to Nicolás Maduro's official social-media accounts on Sunday appear to show the former Venezuelan president smiling and making .
articles.body: Two photographs posted to Nicolás Maduro's official social-media accounts on Sunday appear to show the former Venezuelan president smiling and making peace signs at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, nearly eight months after US forces captured him in Caracas.The pictures show the 63-year-old dressed in a grey sweatshirt and trousers with white shoes. Although released on August 30, timestamps on the photographs indicate they were taken on June 25.“I send these photos as a small gift to all my grandsons and granddaughters, to the boys and girls, and to all the noble people who love us,” Maduro said in an English rendering of his Spanish-language message. He said he and his wife, Cilia Flores, would “remain strong, serene, and confident” and added: “Venezuela will be reborn.” Maduro also described the support reaching the couple as “that love that reaches us transformed into prayer, into constant action, into solidarity and true support.”The June 25 date places the photographs a day after two earthquakes measuring magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck Venezuela. The death toll from the quakes had risen to 6,509 by August 25.Oil deal widens US role in VenezuelaMaduro's message emerged as the government led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez moves into a new phase of relations with Washington, particularly over Venezuela's vast oil reserves.President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business.Rodríguez subsequently said the bilateral energy project would run for 25 years and involve 17 strategic oilfields, with an initial production target of more than 1.5 million barrels a day, news agency Reuters reported.News agency Associated Press separately reported, citing a US official familiar with the agreement, that the new private company had been granted 100-year rights to develop the oilfields.Several important terms have yet to be made public. The US official told AP that the United States would receive 55% of the effective output of the new company through a combination of an ownership stake and rights to buy oil at cost. It remains unclear how much of that share would come from equity ownership and how much from the oil-purchase arrangement.Questions also remain over how the agreement will be financed and implemented, while the identity of the private operator has not been disclosed.Trump said on Sunday that Venezuelan crude obtained through the arrangement would also be used to replenish the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The stockpile held about 290 million barrels on August 21, near its lowest level in 44 years.A substantial increase in Venezuelan production is unlikely to come quickly. The country's oil infrastructure requires major investment, while unresolved financing and legal questions could affect how rapidly companies commit capital.Defence prepares immunity challengeWhile relations between Caracas and Washington have shifted since Maduro's removal, he and Flores remain in US custody awaiting a trial scheduled for June 1, 2027.US forces seized the couple from their Caracas residence during an overnight operation authorised by Trump on January 3 and transferred them to New York. They appeared in federal court two days later and pleaded not guilty.Maduro faces four felony counts, including narcoterrorism conspiracy and conspiracy to import cocaine. Federal prosecutors accuse him of involvement in a scheme to facilitate cocaine shipments to the United States. He could face life in prison if convicted.His lawyer, Barry Pollack, has said he will seek dismissal on the ground that Maduro is immune from prosecution as the head of a sovereign state. Pollack has also previously indicated that the defence may challenge the legality of Maduro's capture.US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein has given the defence until September 2 to file its first round of motions seeking dismissal. Arguments on those motions are scheduled for November 17, while a second round of motions is due by January 11, 2027, after prosecutors turn over additional evidence, some of which is expected to be classified.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal races to rescue trapped workers, as flood death toll surpasses 900
articles.summary: Nepal officials say rescuers focusing on reaching workers in hydropower project tunnels in flood-stricken region.
articles.body:
Nepal’s rescue teams, aided by Chinese and Indian experts, are racing to save more than 900 workers believed to be trapped underground at hydropower projects hit by devastating flash floods.

Nepali officials said on Monday that the focus was on reaching the workers in about a dozen hydropower project tunnels blocked by mud and rock debris.

The unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud and debris on the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday – caused by a glacier collapse – has killed 903 people with 4,247 missing in Nepal, its disaster authority said.

The flood also wreaked havoc across the border in China’s Tibet region, where at least 16 people died and 546 are missing, said Chinese authorities.

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams in Nepal showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud and rocks under lights in the dark of the night as workers watched. Soldiers used torchlights in a big pit they had created to look for space to get into one tunnel.

“A large amount of debris has been deposited and that is posing us a big challenge to open the tunnels,” Nepal army spokesperson, Raja Ram Basnet, told the Reuters news agency.

“Our main focus is on opening the tunnels.”

Hundreds of bodies, many unidentified, have been buried in shallow graves as they began decomposing in the humid weather after being swept down the mountains by the torrent.

At a hospital in the capital of Kathmandu, morgues have reached capacity and families are flocking to other hospitals in hopes of finding missing loved ones , reported Al Jazeera’s Minelle Fernandez.

In addition to the 933 missing hydropower workers, some 500 workers from the Truck and Container Association are also missing, said Fernandez.

The Red Cross has estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the flood was an “unprecedented and devastating natural disaster” and it remained challenging to compile a complete assessment of the damage.

“Despite the adverse weather, difficult terrain and continuing risks, we are moving forward with determination to save the lives of our citizens,” he said in a Facebook post late on Sunday, adding that nearly 21,000 security personnel were involved in rescue operations, besides civilian workers and volunteers.

While accessibility has been restored on many roads and highways, almost “40 kilometres of roads have been absolutely swept away ”, Al Jazeera’s Fernandez said.

“So there are challenges on the ground in getting this aid to communities, but the authorities, as well as the agencies and their networks are working their way through it.”

China’s state-run CCTV said the government has mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least 220 million yuan ($33mn) to support relief efforts. Equipment and supplies have been airdropped to frontline rescuers, while Chinese soldiers used life-detection equipment to look for the missing.

Beijing said 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were unaccounted for in Tibet.

“President Xi Jinping, according to state media, has called for all out efforts to rescue those missing in the mudslide, and this is the second time that the president has made such a call,” said Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing.

“So this seems to be the Chinese leader’s effort to call on people, not only to continue their efforts, but redouble their efforts even as things are looking grimmer and grimmer.”

China has sent nine tunnel rescue experts to Nepal and shared satellite information with Nepalese authorities, said Yu.

Although Nepal has said it does not need foreign help in general search and rescue efforts, it has accepted help from giant neighbours India and China for their expertise in tunnel rescue.

Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake, formed across the Nepal-China border by the disaster, could trigger new flooding after it began overflowing into Nepal’s rivers.

The weather was good on Monday and rescue work continued to pick up pace, said Narendra Pariyar, the district administrator of Rasuwa, one of the two hard-hit districts.

articles.title: Watch: Zohran Mamdani look-alike contest draws hundreds in New York
articles.summary: US News: Hundreds gathered near Washington Square Park on Sunday for a Zohran Mamdani look-alike contest that drew on different phases of the New York mayor's .
articles.body: Hundreds gathered near Washington Square Park on Sunday for a Zohran Mamdani look-alike contest that drew on different phases of the New York mayor's public life, from politics and basketball to cycling and his earlier rap career.Actor and comedian Amadeo Fusca, 40, won the $100 prize in a New York Knicks jersey paired with formalwear, a Mamdani-style haircut and similar facial hair. His outfit echoed one worn by the mayor after the Knicks' NBA Finals victory.There was no judging panel. Each contestant named his favourite pizza before the crowd settled the result by applause.Contestants recreate Mamdani's campaign and cycling looksSilver rings, red-and-black ties and variations on dark formalwear appeared across the field, while some entrants drew on the brown suit Mamdani wore during his 2025 mayoral campaign.Others added bicycle helmets, referencing a more recent episode involving the mayor. Mamdani began wearing one earlier in August after facing criticism for cycling without a helmet.One entrant wore an apron with no shirt, drawing on imagery from Mamdani's 2019 Mr. Cardamom era.Permit issue moves contest outside parkA permit issue forced a change of venue. The gathering began inside Washington Square Park, but police moved it beyond the park boundary because no permit had been obtained. Sonder, a social platform for meeting new people, sponsored the event.Mamdani, a democratic socialist whose political agenda has focused on New York's working class, took office in January and has built a substantial following among younger residents and on social media.Sunday's contest was not the first devoted to him. A similar event was held in Brooklyn during his 2025 run for City Hall.Washington Square Park has also hosted other look-alike competitions. In June, five-year-old Knicks fan Francisco won $5,000 at a Jalen Brunson look-alike contest there and received a surprise FaceTime call from Brunson, the NBA Finals MVP.Mamdani impersonation becomes paying workFusca had already turned his resemblance to Mamdani into a recurring act before entering Sunday's contest. The actor, who has appeared in episodes of “NCIS” and the film “The Alto Knights,” has drawn millions of views with social-media sketches impersonating the mayor.He said the act began during Mamdani's mayoral campaign, when friends repeatedly sent him photographs pointing out their resemblance. “It was kind of the perfect storm of people constantly hitting me up,” Fusca told the New York Post after his win.At first, he was reluctant to alter his appearance, particularly because he had been growing his hair.“The funny thing is, I was growing my hair, and I was like, ‘No, I’m growing my hair, I don’t really want to do that.’ And then when [Mamdani] won [the mayor’s race], it was just insane, the messages I was getting,” he said. “I went to the barber that morning and said, ‘Here, cut my hair, and make me look like this now.’ And like, I have to look like this all the time now!”The impersonation later began drawing attention at Knicks watch parties. Fusca, who lives only a few blocks from Gracie Mansion on Manhattan's Upper East Side, said the reactions exceeded what he had expected. “People were reacting like crazy, beyond what I even thought,” he said. “We just kept going to watch parties, and I kept inhabiting this field of people. It’s crazy how happy people get.”The attention has also begun translating into professional work. “I started doing Instagram videos to parody him and take on his shape,” Fusca said. “It started to get more love, and I sort of realized recently that people are hiring me to do their variety shows.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Two Canadian builders turned 612,000 recycled plastic bottles into a 2,000-sq-ft home; its panels were tested to withstand sustained winds of 326 mph, twice Category 5 hurricane strength
articles.summary: Rest of World News: What if hundreds of thousands of plastic bottles destined for a landfill could instead become the walls of a home? In a small community in Nova Scotia.
articles.body: What if hundreds of thousands of plastic bottles destined for a landfill could instead become the walls of a home? In a small community in Nova Scotia, two Canadian builders turned that idea into a real house. Built in Meteghan River, the approximately 2,000-square-foot home uses composite panels made from recycled plastic bottles, giving discarded polyethylene terephthalate (PET) a very different second life. The unusual structure was created not simply as an architectural experiment, but as an attempt to demonstrate how recycled materials could be used in practical construction. Its makers also wanted to explore whether the same technology could eventually be adapted for smaller homes, emergency shelters and buildings designed for areas exposed to severe weather.According to The Chronicle Herald, Nova Scotia builders Joel German and David Saulnier created the house using around 612,000 recycled plastic bottles. Invest Nova Scotia also documented the project and explained how the bottles were transformed into PET foam panels for the home's construction.From plastic bottles to wallsThe bottles did not simply become part of the house in their original form. Instead, they were processed into a specialised material that could be incorporated into structural composite panels. JD Composites, the Nova Scotia company founded by builders Joel German and David Saulnier, worked with Ontario-based Armacell, which processed the recycled bottles into PET foam. According to Invest Nova Scotia, the bottles were mulched and melted into small beads before being put through an extrusion process that produced foam with the density required for different applications. In this case, the resulting material formed the core of the panels for the house. That meant the finished building could look much like a conventional modern home despite having an unusual material hidden within its walls.The recycled plastic was essentially transformed from a waste product into a construction component. The approach also reflected the founders' experience with composite materials. Rather than developing a house that depended on plastic bottles being visibly incorporated into its design, German and Saulnier focused on turning recycled PET into a usable building material. The result was a three-bedroom concept home in Meteghan River. The house was intended to demonstrate what the material could do while allowing the builders to observe how the various components performed over time.Built for extreme conditionsOne of the most remarkable aspects of the project was the strength demonstrated by its panels. An individual 8-by-8-foot panel was subjected to wind testing and reportedly withstood speeds of 326 mph (524 km/h). That is roughly twice the wind speed associated with a Category 5 hurricane. The result highlighted the potential strength of the recycled-PET composite material. However, the distinction between the panel test and the finished house is important. The 326-mph figure should not be interpreted as meaning the entire completed 2,000-square-foot home was placed in a wind tunnel and proven capable of surviving a 326-mph storm. The test concerned a structural panel used in the building.The material also offered insulation and durability advantages. PET foam can provide thermal insulation, while the composite construction was intended to resist issues associated with conventional building materials. The project therefore combined the environmental objective of recycling plastic with an effort to develop a lightweight and durable construction system. Invest Nova Scotia reported that the company's engineers had double-checked aspects of the construction, while the builders planned to continue monitoring the home and observing how materials such as paints and primers performed over time.More than a one-off homeFor German and Saulnier, the house was never intended to be simply an unusual private residence. It was designed as a demonstration of what could potentially be done with recycled plastic on a larger scale. JD Composites was interested in applications including smaller dwellings, shelters, sheds, offices, sleeping barracks and disaster-relief structures. The company also explored possibilities such as hurricane-resistant housing and tiny homes. That focus on scalable construction was important because the environmental impact of a single experimental house is limited. But the idea changes considerably if the same material can be used to construct multiple buildings. The project's most striking statistic was therefore not just the size of the house, but the amount of plastic diverted into it. About 612,000 bottles were used to construct the building, according to the project accounts. The Meteghan River house ultimately became an example of how recycling can move beyond familiar products such as clothing, carpeting and consumer goods. Here, discarded plastic was transformed into a component of a functioning home.For the builders, the experiment raised a larger possibility: that plastic waste could become part of the solution to another pressing challenge, creating durable, efficient and rapidly deployable buildings. The house did not prove that recycled plastic can replace every conventional construction material, but it demonstrated how a material normally regarded as waste could be engineered into something strong enough to form the shell of a home.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Syria is choosing diplomacy with Israel, but can its approach last?
articles.summary: Israel has attacked Syria, occupied its south since the al-Assad regime’s ouster, testing Syria’s diplomatic outreach.
articles.body:
Ever since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government, Syria has chosen diplomatic engagement with Israel over military confrontation.

As Syria’s new government attempts to rebuild the country after more than a decade of war, the country’s officials have committed themselves to a policy of avoiding conflicts with their neighbours.

Yet Israel continues to disrupt any efforts at a more sustained peace agreement, including through repeated attacks on Syrian soil. But analysts told Al Jazeera that despite these provocations, Damascus sees the diplomatic track as its only choice.

“Syria’s government is intensely pragmatic in that it’s willing to basically sit down and talk to and do deals with people as long as it promotes Syria’s national interest,” Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer on security studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera.

Under the al-Assad presidency, Syria was a part of the Iran-driven “axis of resistance” that also included other allies of Tehran. Syrian territory was used to transport weapons and financial aid from Iran to Tehran’s Lebanese allies, Hezbollah.

The Syrian military itself, however, has not engaged militarily with Israel since a 1974 disengagement agreement signed under Bashar’s father and predecessor, Hafez al-Assad.

When rebels led by current President Ahmed al-Sharaa took Damascus and deposed the al-Assad government in December 2024, Israel instantly responded by attacking Syria’s military infrastructure around the country. Israeli troops also moved further into parts of southern Syria, beyond the occupied Golan Heights. Almost two years later, Israeli troops continue to set up checkpoints and harass and arrest Syrian citizens in these parts of the country.

Since then, Syrian officials, including President al-Sharaa, have said they have no intent to attack Israel and that they seek peace with all their neighbours. Still, Israel has threatened the Syrian government on numerous occasions, warning them not to deploy military troops in southern Syria and even bombing the Syrian Ministry of Defence in Damascus in July 2025.

“The government has to walk a tightrope as ever,” Geist Pinfold said. “There seems to be a feeling in Syria that Syrians are tired of war, they’re tired of conflict, they want stability, they want to be able to grow, they want to practise nation building.”

Damascus has responded to the numerous aggressions by seeking regional and international help. Syria’s new government has gained the trust of Donald Trump’s administration in the US and has close ties with Turkiye and numerous Gulf states. Continued Israeli aggressions and violations have not deterred Syria’s efforts at diplomacy either.

“The Syrian government is hoping that it can basically leverage its pragmatism to create stability in Syria by basically removing Israel as the key spoiler at the moment in contemporary post-Assad Syria,” Geist Pinfold said. “It hasn’t been able to do that so far simply because under the Netanyahu administration, Israel seems more willing to live by the sword.”

While Damascus has said it is committed to peace and diplomacy, it has also made clear it does not yet view Israel as a reliable neighbour. Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani told the Reuters news agency: “We do not trust Israel currently.”

Syria has also filed multiple complaints with the United Nations regarding Israel.

“Damascus does not currently consider Israel a trustworthy political partner, but it views negotiations with it as a security necessity,” Souhayb Jawhar, a Lebanese analyst with Badil, a Beirut-based think tank, told Al Jazeera.

Jawhar said Damascus has three immediate demands, which include stopping Israeli strikes on Syrian territory, stopping Israeli incursions into Syrian territory and the arrests of Syrian citizens, and forcing Israel to withdraw its troops from the areas it seized after the fall of al-Assad.

“After years of war, Syrians are exhausted and certainly not interested in another war,” Bente Scheller, head of Heinrich-Boll-Stiftung’s Middle East and North Africa Division, told Al Jazeera. “However, Israel acting with impunity in Syria creates hard feelings and undermines support for normalisation or even peace.”

Until now, Syria appears to believe that the alternative to diplomacy with Israel, even in the face of Israeli attacks, could be too costly, particularly for a country still rebuilding after several devastating years of war.

“[Diplomacy] is the least costly option for Damascus,” Jawhar said. “The Syrian leadership does not want to open a military front with Israel while it is rebuilding its army, state and economy. It is also counting on the United States to impose constraints on Israeli behaviour.”

Al-Shaibani met with Roman Gofman , the head of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency, in US-mediated talks in Amman recently. Syria’s state media agency SANA said the talks “focused on establishing practical mechanisms to halt Israeli attacks, arrests and targeting operations” and “reviving negotiations for a lasting security agreement between the two sides”.

The talks came on the back of an Israeli attack on a Syrian airbase near Idlib , in northwest Syria, though the two sides had reportedly also met shortly before that attack. Analysts said the attacks were likely a message to Syria about efforts to rebuild their air force and to Turkiye, whose zone of influence extends across northern Syria.

But despite Israel’s belligerence, analysts said Syrians generally are supportive of the government’s efforts to avoid conflict and apply pressure on the Israelis via regional and international allies.

“There seems to be a popular appetite for Israel to basically go away and stop being a threat and stop being a spoiler,” Geist Pinfold said. “That does not mean that there’s a popular appetite, for example, for Syria to give up its claim to the Golan Heights.”

The issue of the Golan Heights has particular relevance in Syria. The area was originally occupied by Israel in 1967 and Israeli troops further advanced in the Golan after the fall of al-Assad in December 2024. Israel has said repeatedly they do not intend to give up the Golan Heights, which also gives Israel a direct flight path to attack Iran, Geist Pinfold pointed out.

And with October’s elections approaching in Israel, many analysts said Benjamin Netanyahu’s government may look to raise tensions on Israel’s many fronts, including possibly in Syria, rather than ease them.

“There’s this understanding that coming to an agreement [with Syria] could actually be worse for Israel’s national interests,” Geist Pinfold said. “Whereas if it doesn’t agree to anything, it can’t be accused of breaking anything. And also it gives Israel more operational freedoms.”

After Israel’s attack on the airbase, US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack proposed the creation of a deconfliction mechanism that would include Turkiye, Syria and Israel.

The mechanism follows other such US-led efforts in Lebanon and between Israel and Syria in Amman. Analysts, however, said such a mechanism was unlikely to be effective without concerted US pressure on Israel .

“The recent bombardments of Abu al-Duhur airbase despite intense talks the days before show that the current Israeli government values military means over a political process and does not hesitate to act against Trump’s plans,” Scheller said.

Despite declared ceasefires or efforts at de-escalation, Israel continues attacks on people, including civilians, in Gaza, the occupied West Bank, Lebanon and Syria. And analysts believe it has a new enemy in its crosshairs.

“The big new scary bogeyman on the horizon is Turkiye,” Geist Pinfold said.

“Netanyahu’s been talking about it, leaders of the opposition, particularly Naftali Bennett, have been saying Israel needs to reorient its foreign policy and security policies towards confronting Turkiye. So it is very much the next big threat on the horizon.”

Against that backdrop, analysts said there was little likelihood of a genuine peace agreement anytime soon.

“The problem at the moment is there just is not a receptive partner [in Israel],” Geist Pinfold said. “The Syrian government seems determined to use diplomacy to convince Israel that it is not a threat and that it can be negotiated with rather than basically Israel unilaterally imposing its will by force, but at the moment there’s just simply no receptive audience for that.”
